title: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment No 3) Bill
what_it_is: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment No 3) Bill

sections.label: Debate on marriage and 377A
sections.summary: This allows a holistic debate on both Bills, with a formal Second Reading of the Penal Code (Amendment) Bill, giving effect to the Prime Minister's National Day Rally announcements on marriage and section 377A.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This will allow a holistic debate and enable Members to raise questions or express their views on both Bills during the debate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will still have the formal Second Reading of the Penal Code (Amendment) Bill to ensure that procedural requirements are dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This Bill gives effect to what Prime Minister announced at this year’s National Day Rally, that is, the Government will protect the definition of marriage from being challenged in the Courts on constitutional grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Prime Minister had also announced that the Government will repeal section 377A of the Penal Code.

sections.label: Marriage and family policies
sections.summary: Policies reflect and reinforce marriage and family; the Government does not support same-sex family formation and maintains its policy against planned and deliberate single parenthood, including ART or surrogacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Governments will come, governments will go, but this endures." Hence, our policies also reflect and reinforce this basic idea about marriage and family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We do not support same-sex family formation and we maintain our policy against planned and deliberate single parenthood, including using assisted reproduction techniques (ART) or surrogacy.

sections.label: Adoption and same-sex families
sections.summary: Adoption should not support the formation of same-sex families, and Singapore's public policy is to uphold heterosexual marriage and promote families within such marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Adoption should not be used as a process to support the formation of same-sex families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I reiterate today: Singapore's public policy is and has always been to uphold heterosexual marriage and promote the formation of families within such marriages.

sections.label: Policies relying on marriage definition
sections.summary: Housing, financial benefits, ART, adoption, education and media are examples of policies and measures that rely on the definition of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Examples of these policies and measures that rely on the definition of marriage are: housing, where public housing subsidies and access are prioritised for married couples; financial benefits that favour married couples, such as the Baby Bonus Cash Gift; ART, where access to IVF and use of frozen gametes for procreation are only allowed for married persons; adoption, where only married couples can apply jointly; education, where what is taught in preschools and MOE schools would be based on marriage as between a man and a woman and such a family as the basic unit of society; and media, where higher age ratings apply for media content which depicts non-traditional family units, such as same-sex families.

sections.label: Safeguarding marriage from court challenges
sections.summary: Court decisions change things overnight with drastic social repercussions, so the institution of marriage and related laws and policies are being proactively safeguarded from court challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: When the courts decide, things change overnight, with drastic social repercussions that polarise society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Hence, we are proactively safeguarding the institution of marriage and related laws and policies from being challenged in Court.

sections.label: Necessity of the amendment now
sections.summary: Inaction might be politically expedient but not right or responsible; there is a significant risk of laws being struck down, so this amendment is necessary now and not delayed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To use that as a reason for inaction might be politically expedient but it would not be the right or responsible thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have assessed that there is a significant risk to our laws being struck down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This amendment is necessary and it is the right thing to deal with it now and not delay.

sections.label: New Article 156 on marriage
sections.summary: A new Article 156 lets Parliament act to define, regulate, protect, safeguard, support, foster and promote marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It allows the political process to balance different interests and perspectives and does not pass the buck to the Court to rule on social issues which are best dealt with via Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: There will be a new Article 156, under the General Provisions of the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Clause 1 of the Article makes clear that Parliament can act to define, regulate, protect, safeguard, support, foster and promote marriage.

sections.label: Clause 3(a) marriage definition
sections.summary: Clause 3(a) states that nothing in Part 4, the eight fundamental liberties, invalidates a legislative definition of marriage as a union between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Clause 3(a) provides that nothing in Part 4 of the Constitution, which sets out the eight fundamental liberties, will invalidate any legislative definition of marriage as a union between a man and a woman.

sections.label: Strongest protection for heterosexual marriage
sections.summary: For Article 156(3) and (4), the balance struck favours the strongest protection for Parliament's heterosexual definition of marriage and related laws and policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In the case of Article 156(3) and (4), we have struck the balance in favour of having the strongest protection for the heterosexual definition of marriage adopted by Parliament, and the ability of Parliament and the Government to make laws and policies on the basis of this definition.

sections.label: Marriage not a fundamental right
sections.summary: The view is that elevating marriage to the same level as fundamental rights in the Constitution would not be appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Our view is that elevating marriage to the same level as fundamental rights in the Constitution would not be appropriate.

sections.label: Future Parliaments may amend marriage definition
sections.summary: The definition of marriage remains in the Women's Charter, Interpretation Act and AMLA, and the constitutional amendment will not prevent future Governments from amending it by simple majority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The definition of marriage is and will remain in the Women’s Charter, Interpretation Act and AMLA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Importantly, this Government will not use our current super-majority in Parliament to tie the hands of the future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Hence, the constitutional amendment will not prevent future Governments, elected by the people, from amending the legal definition of marriage by a simple majority in Parliament, should they choose to do so.

sections.label: Lawrence Wong on not changing definition
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, as the 4G leader, said the Government will not change them under his watch if the PAP win the next General Election.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, as the 4G leader, has also said that the Government will not change them under his watch if the PAP were to win the next General Election.

sections.label: Repeal engagement with Malay/Muslim community
sections.summary: The Government shared its intention to repeal section 377A and engaged the Malay/Muslim community extensively this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: (In Malay):   In sharing the Government's intention to repeal section 377A, we have engaged the Malay/Muslim community extensively throughout this year.

sections.label: Repeal with constitutional amendment
sections.summary: Repeal of section 377A will be accompanied by a simultaneous constitutional amendment so Parliament keeps the right to determine marriage and family laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It is clear that as a society, we want the institution of family to remain the central pillar of our community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I have explained that the repeal of section 377A will be accompanied by a constitutional amendment that will be done simultaneously, so that Parliament continues to have the right to determine marriage and family laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The amendments protect these laws and policies from new challenges based on Part 4 of the Constitution such as the frequent challenges to section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This also means that other benefits that takes reference from our definition of marriage, including public housing subsidies and priority access for married couples as well as financial incentives for married couples to have children such as the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, will remain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The guidance from our Mufti and established scholars has clarified the religious position on homosexuality in a judicious manner – that in Islam, only sexual relations between man and woman in marriage are permitted.

sections.label: Respect among citizens
sections.summary: Singaporeans must respect each other as fellow citizens in exercising this right, and pro-family values are not majoritarian or religious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As Singaporeans, we must also have respect for each other as fellow citizens in exercising this right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I want to make clear that our pro-family values and position are not a result of a majoritarian or a religious approach.

sections.label: Political accommodation balancing views
sections.summary: A political accommodation balances different legitimate views among Singaporeans without tying a future Parliament's hands, with Parliament as the main platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister has said, we are seeking a political accommodation that balances different legitimate views and aspirations among Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: However, it is also done in a way to not tie the hands of a future Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Above all, we want to ensure that the Parliament should be the main platform to discuss sensitive issues and not the Courts.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: The speaker will speak on the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code, which was thought about very carefully.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I will now speak on the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We thought very carefully before moving on the repeal of this section.

sections.label: Section 377A offence and history
sections.summary: Section 377A makes it an offence for a male person to commit gross indecency with another male, introduced in 1938 under British colonial rule.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As Members will know, section 377A makes it an offence for a male person, whether in public or private, to commit any act of gross indecency with another male.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The section was introduced in 1938 when Singapore was a British colony.

sections.label: UK Commons late-night amendment
sections.summary: The measure was introduced in the UK House of Commons at 2.30 am as a last-minute amendment to an unrelated bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: What we did find, was that it was introduced in the UK House of Commons at 2.30 am in the morning with very few members of parliament who were present, as a last-minute amendment to an entirely unrelated bill.

sections.label: Other UK homosexual offences
sections.summary: Besides section 11 of the UKCL, the UK had three other offences sometimes used to prosecute homosexual conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In addition to section 11 of the UKCL, the UK also had three other offences which were also used sometimes to prosecute homosexual conduct.

sections.label: Origins of sodomy offence
sections.summary: The offence of sodomy was introduced as part of a power struggle between Henry and the Catholic church.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When you go through this history into the origins of the offence of sodomy, we see that it was introduced as part of a power struggle between Henry and the Catholic church, and not because of any view that sodomy per se ought to be criminalised.

sections.label: Wolfenden Committee appointed 1954
sections.summary: The UK government appointed the Wolfenden Committee in August 1954 to review laws on homosexual offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The UK government appointed a committee known as the Wolfenden Committee in August 1954 to review laws relating to homosexual offences.

sections.label: Committee on private homosexual activities
sections.summary: The committee took the view that homosexual activities in private should not be criminalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The committee took the view that homosexual activities in private should not be criminalised.

sections.label: UK 1967 decriminalisation vote
sections.summary: In 1967, the UK parliament voted to decriminalise private consensual homosexual sex between two adults.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 1967, the UK parliament voted to decriminalise private consensual homosexual sex between two adults.

sections.label: UK homosexual law repeal
sections.summary: In 2003, all UK laws specifically criminalising male homosexual behaviour, including gross indecency, were fully repealed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2003, all of the UK’s laws that specifically criminalised male homosexual behaviour, including the offence of gross indecency, were fully repealed.

sections.label: European court decriminalisation ruling
sections.summary: In 1981 the European Court of Human Rights found criminalising private homosexual conduct between men breached the European Convention on Human Rights, and the UK parliament decriminalised it in Northern Ireland in 1982.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: After 14 years, in 1981, the European Court of Human Rights found that criminalising private homosexual conduct between men was “an unjustified interference with   right to respect for his private life” and was a breach of the European Convention on Human Rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The UK was bound by that decision and the UK parliament decriminalised private, consensual homosexual conduct between adults in Northern Ireland in 1982.

sections.label: Texas Republican anti-LGBT platform
sections.summary: The Republican Party of Texas recently adopted anti-LGBT positions into their party platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Republican Party of Texas recently adopted anti-LGBT positions into their party platform.

sections.label: Survey on same-sex marriage
sections.summary: A March survey of more than 22,000 people by the Public Religion Research Institute found 48% supported same-sex marriage and 50% opposed it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A survey of more than 22,000 people by the Public Religion Research Institute in March of this year found that 48% supported same-sex marriage and 50% opposed it.

sections.label: US embassy LGBT webinar
sections.summary: In 2021, the US embassy co-hosted a webinar on LGBT rights with a Singaporean LGBT organisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, in 2021, the US embassy co-hosted a webinar on LGBT rights with a Singaporean LGBT organisation.

sections.label: Prime Minister on section 377A
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said we will try to maintain a balance upholding traditional heterosexual family values with space for homosexuals, and will retain section 377A but not proactively enforce it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will try and maintain a balance, said the Prime Minister, to uphold a stable society with traditional, heterosexual family values, but with space for homosexuals to live their lives and contribute to society.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He added that we would continue to retain section 377A but not proactively enforce it.

sections.label: Legal risk to section 377A
sections.summary: There is a significant legal risk that the Courts will strike down section 377A if nothing is done.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, there is a significant legal risk that the Courts will strike down section 377A if we left it alone and did nothing.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: After repeal, only consensual, male adult homosexual conduct in private will no longer be an offence, and the time has come to remove section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The only thing that will no longer be an offence after the repeal is consensual, male adult homosexual conduct conducted in private.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The time has come for us to remove section 377A.

sections.label: Removing section 377A
sections.summary: Section 377A should no longer be in our books.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Section 377A should no longer be in our books.

sections.label: Court of Appeal on Constitution
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal said section 377A did not contravene Article 9 or Article 12 of the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the substantive issue, the Court of Appeal said that section 377A did not contravene either Article 9 or Article 12 of the Constitution.

sections.label: Tan Seng Kee appeal dismissed
sections.summary: In Tan Seng Kee, the appeal was dismissed on procedural grounds because the applicants lacked locus standi to challenge section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: How and why the Court of Appeal came to that decision and what it said is important.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This time in Tan Seng Kee, the appeal was dismissed on procedural grounds, on the basis that the applicants lacked locus standi to challenge section 377A.

sections.label: Locus standi and unenforceability
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal said there was no locus standi because the Attorney-General said there would generally be no prosecution, making section 377A unenforceable until clear notice of enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal said that there was no locus standi because the Attorney-General had said that, absent other factors, there would generally be no prosecution under section 377A, where the conduct was between two consenting adults in a private place.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On this basis, the Court of Appeal said that section 377A was unenforceable until the Attorney-General gave clear notice that he intended to enforce section 377A.

sections.label: Court of Appeal on section 377A
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal's reasoning suggests section 377A is probably unconstitutional if the Syed Suhail test is applied.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you see what the Court of Appeal has said: "One could then conclude that the differentia embodied in section 377A (namely, male-male sex acts) lacks a rational relation to legislative object of reflecting societal disapproval of homosexual conduct in general or safeguarding public morality generally." In plain language, what this means is section 377A is probably unconstitutional, if the Syed Suhail test is to be applied.

sections.label: Locus standi and section 377A
sections.summary: If the Syed Suhail test is applied section 377A is likely struck down, but no one has locus standi to challenge it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It means that if another constitutional challenge against section 377A is brought before the Court, the Syed Suhail test is likely to be applied.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if that test is applied, section 377A is likely to be struck down on the grounds that it breaches Article 12 of the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But the Court of Appeal in Tan Seng Kee this year also said there is no locus standi to bring the challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, as long as the Attorney-General maintains the current position and does not re-assert the right to prosecute cases under section 377A, then there should be no risk that section 377A would be found unconstitutional because no one would have standing to challenge it in the first place.

sections.label: Past convicts may have standing
sections.summary: Persons previously convicted under section 377A may have a case for standing, as a personal view.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, persons who had been convicted in the past under section 377A, they may well have a case for standing – I do not want my speech to be read as giving a right to people; it is my personal view.

sections.label: Government advice on section 377A risk
sections.summary: The Attorney-General and the speaker advised the Government that section 377A is at significant risk of being struck down in a future challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As the Attorney-General and I looked carefully at the Tan Seng Kee judgment and as the Prime Minister said during the National Day Rally, the Attorney-General and I have advised the Government that in a future Court challenge, there is a significant risk of section 377A being struck down.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, let us be clear: one, after the Tan Seng Kee judgment, section 377A is at significant risk of being struck down in a future challenge; and two, we cannot simply hope that the point on locus standi is enough for the Government and Parliament to do nothing.

sections.label: Marriage laws could be at risk
sections.summary: If the Courts strike down section 377A, laws defining marriage as between a man and a woman could also be at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And what can happen if the Courts strike down section 377A?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Then, our laws defining marriage as being between a man and a woman, and our laws and policies based on that definition, could also be at risk sometime in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, the heterosexual definition of marriage could be challenged on the basis that it is against Article 12 of the Constitution.

sections.label: Court of Appeal on 2007 compromise
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal said the 2007 compromise was political but legal standards may still judge section 377A's constitutionality.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Members may know, the Court of Appeal has also said that although the 2007 compromise was inherently political, legal standards do still exist and may be applied to judge the legality or constitutionality of section 377A.

sections.label: Duty to act in Parliament
sections.summary: The passage states it is Parliament's duty to act on laws at risk of being found unconstitutional, as avoiding this would harm society.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we see a risk that a law may be found unconstitutional, it is our duty to act and deal with it in Parliament, both because it is our duty to do so and because taking the easy way out would have serious negative consequences for our society.

sections.label: Court versus Parliament on 377A
sections.summary: The passage says a court striking down section 377A could not consider effects on marriage, while Parliament proposes constitutional amendments protecting heterosexual marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If they strike down section 377A, they will do so without being able to consider the consequential effects of that decision on the definition of marriage, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Whereas, in Parliament, we are now proposing amendments to the Constitution to further protect heterosexual marriage.

sections.label: Courage to do what is right
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Members are prepared to take steps to safeguard society and urges them to do their duty in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The question is: are we prepared to take the appropriate steps to save and safeguard what is important for our society, whether we have the courage of our conviction, which should be to do what is good for Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, Mr Speaker, I say to all Members, let us do what is right, do our duty, what is expected of us in Parliament and take a path forward on this difficult issue.

sections.label: Workers' Party MPs' differing views
sections.summary: The passage states that Workers' Party MPs, speaking in their individual capacities, hold different views on repealing section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Speaking in their individual capacities, the Workers' Party Members of Parliament (MPs) have different views on the repeal of section 377A.

sections.label: Lifting the party whip
sections.summary: The passage states the whip is lifted for Workers' Party MPs so those against repeal can vote freely and represent Singaporeans with religious and conscience concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Not lifting the whip would deny Workers' Party MPs not in favour of a repeal of 377A the opportunity to vote freely and in doing so, to also represent Singaporeans who see this issue as a matter of deep religious belief and conscience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I have decided to lift the whip for the Workers' Party MPs.

sections.label: Two MPs absent with COVID-19
sections.summary: The passage records that MPs Muhamad Faisal bin Abdul Manap and Chua Kheng Wee Louis are absent with COVID-19, with Faisal against repeal and Chua for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the record, Mr Speaker, both MPs Muhamad Faisal bin Abdul Manap and Chua Kheng Wee Louis are not present for this debate as they are COVID-19 positive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Faisal disagrees with the repeal of 377A as a matter of religion and conscience while Mr Chua agrees to the repeal.

sections.label: 377A amendment in 2007
sections.summary: The passage notes that when section 377A was amended in 2007, other sex acts some find unorthodox were decriminalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One may argue that 377A is much more complex, that not regulating sexual practices has greater social consequences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But let us remember that when section 377A of the Penal Code was amended in 2007, it decriminalised other sex acts that some still find unorthodox.

sections.label: Court judgment and repeal decision
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal judgment in Tan Seng Kee vs Attorney-General appears to have precipitated the Government's decision to repeal 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the main, the Court of Appeal judgment in Tan Seng Kee vs Attorney-General appears to have precipitated the Government's decision to repeal 377A.

sections.label: Protecting marriage from constitutional challenge
sections.summary: The speaker sees the decision to protect marriage from constitutional challenge as an institution between man and woman only through a narrow lens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Likewise, I see the decision to protect marriage from constitutional challenge as an institution between man and woman only, through a very narrow lens.

sections.label: Repeal and religious Singaporeans
sections.summary: In repealing 377A, religious Singaporeans are not asked to endorse homosexuality but to honour equality of all Singaporeans in law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In repealing 377A, religious Singaporeans are not asked to endorse homosexuality but instead honour the equality of all Singaporeans in the eyes of the law – that no consenting adult should be regarded as criminals because of what they do in private.

sections.label: Secular politics and harmonious living
sections.summary: The passage states there is no basis to feel cancelled if views are not set as expectations for all society, and there must be a secular approach to politics and governance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is no basis for us to feel cancelled, provided our views are not set as an expectation for all society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There must be a secular approach to politics and governance, even as we celebrate and protect the freedom of religion in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party cannot conceive of any other way for different groups and religious communities to live harmoniously with each other in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But as with most difficult conversations in search of a landing point, it will be crucial to adopt a gentler tone and enlightened perspective that extends and considers the impact on broader community and society, and most fundamentally, a spirit of empathy.

sections.label: 2018 CNA interview views
sections.summary: The speaker had already articulated views on this matter in 2018 when interviewed by CNA, stating support for repeal of section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is because I had already articulated my views on this matter in 2018 when I was interviewed by CNA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Then, I stated my support for the repeal of section 377A.

sections.label: Holistic review before legislative decision
sections.summary: The speaker advocated a holistic review before any legislative decision, to address concerns that repealing section 377A may affect marriage and family, and supports the Bills' provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I also advocated a holistic review of the matter, before any legislative decision is made, to address the legitimate concerns that the repeal of section 377A may have an impact on important institutions such as marriage and family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I therefore have no hesitation in supporting the carefully calibrated provisions in these Bills today.

sections.label: Constitutional amendments and marriage
sections.summary: The constitutional amendments make clear that repealing section 377A will not affect marriage between a man and a woman or Government policies promoting traditional families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the same time, the amendments to the Constitution in this House makes it clear that the repeal of section 377A will not affect the important institution of marriage, as between a man and a woman, and the Government policies promoting traditional families.

sections.label: TODAY Youth Survey 2022
sections.summary: A TODAY Youth Survey 2022 found about two-thirds of young adults agreed repealing a law criminalising gay sex is a step towards a more inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Based on the TODAY Youth Survey 2022 published in TODAY on 15 November 2022, about two-thirds of our young adults agreed that the repeal of a law criminalising gay sex represents a step towards a more inclusive society.

sections.label: Legitimacy of democratic system
sections.summary: The passage states it is about upholding the legitimacy of the democratic system of Government in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, it is about upholding the legitimacy of the democratic system of Government that we have in Singapore.

sections.label: US abortion right overturned
sections.summary: In the US, a federal right to abort established in a 1973 case was overturned by a US Supreme Court majority, restoring states' power to outlaw abortion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the US, we saw the swinging of the pendulum from one end to the other just about five months ago when the federal right of choice to abort, established in a 1973 case, was overturned by a majority in the US supreme court in favour of restoring the states' power to outlaw abortion.

sections.label: Singapore gay man adoption case
sections.summary: In 2018, the Singapore High Court allowed a gay man to adopt a son he fathered through a surrogate mother, as no policy against surrogacy existed then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2018, the Singapore High Court decided to allow a Singaporean gay man to adopt a son he fathered through a surrogate mother by paying her US$200,000, because amongst others, the Singapore Government had not promulgated then a policy against surrogacy.

sections.label: Constitution, courts, marriage definition
sections.summary: The Constitution protects rights by letting Courts strike down legislation, and it is proposed that Part 4 be excluded for laws defining marriage as between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The basic idea in this Constitution is to protect individuals' rights by vesting in the Courts the power to strike down legislation passed by this House or Government action should they offend the fundamental liberties stated in this Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is proposed that the entire Part 4 be excluded from application in relation to both a law that defines marriage as a union between a man and a woman, and an exercise of executive authority based on such a definition of marriage.

sections.label: Equality and marriage definition
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Minister's views, saying this reflects Singapore's collective will towards equality and the agreement that marriage is between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would welcome the hon Minister's views on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It reflects Singapore's collective will towards equality as well as the values and realities of our times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We have also, at the same time, captured the wide agreement that marriage is a union between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is an elegant accommodation and a uniquely Singapore way, using hon Minister Masagos' words, of expressing the will of our people through this House.

sections.label: Article 156 marriage challenges
sections.summary: Article 156(3) and (4) state that laws and policies based on marriage as between a man and a woman cannot be invalidated for violating Part 4, for past, current and future laws.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second half of Article 156, namely sub-articles (3) and (4), declare that laws and policies based on a definition of marriage as between a man and a woman cannot be invalidated on the grounds that they violate Part 4 of the Constitution on Fundamental Liberties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is further stated in these two sub-articles that the apparent prohibition of a Constitutional challenge will apply to laws and policies that are in force whether before, on or after the commencement of this Bill, that is, for all past, current and future laws and policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I see Article 156 as the Government's way of signalling that the definition of marriage in Singapore would not be changed in the near future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, as pointed out by the Law Minister in August, this does not amount to an entrenchment of the definition of marriage as between a man and woman.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He and Mr Masagos also made clear earlier that it was open to Parliament to change the definition of marriage by amending the law by a simple majority in Parliament.

sections.label: Concerns over judicial oversight carve-out
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about the new carve-out, the Courts being curtailed in checking Parliament and the Government, and a precedent for future carve-outs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, I am very concerned about the implications of this new carve-out and what Parliament is asked to do today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for Articles 156(3) and (4), I am concerned about the Courts being further curtailed in their constitutional duty to check Parliament and the Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am also concerned about whether the carve-out of judicial oversight on the institution of marriage will set a precedent for future carve-outs, even if this is not the intention today.

sections.label: Abstention vote on Amendment Bill
sections.summary: For the reasons stated, the speaker has decided to abstain on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the reasons I have stated, I have decided to cast a vote of abstention on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill.

sections.label: Risk section 377A struck down
sections.summary: The speaker thought long and hard and agrees there is a significant risk that section 377A will be struck down by the Courts in a future legal challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These are views that must be taken seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I have thought long and hard about this matter, and agree that there is a significant risk that section 377A will be struck down by the Courts in a future legal challenge.

sections.label: Bill on marriage definition
sections.summary: The Bill lets the legislature define and promote marriage, and clause 3 says no law is invalid for defining marriage as a union between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Bill states, "the legislature may, by law, define, regulate, protect, safeguard, support, foster and promote the institution of marriage".

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And then clause 3 states, "nothing in Part 4 invalidates a law enacted before, on or after the date of commencement of this Bill by reason that the law defines marriage as a union between a man and a woman".

sections.label: Policies Prime Minister mentioned
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said in the National Day Rally this includes policies on public housing, education, adoption regulations, advertising standards and film classification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister has said in the National Day Rally, this includes policies on public housing, education, adoption regulations, advertising standards and film classification.

sections.label: Media, housing, library, civil unions
sections.summary: High age ratings apply to media with homosexual content, housing prioritises married couples meaning a man and a woman, children's library books should not depict homosexual unions, and civil unions are not recognised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Four, high age ratings will apply to all media that contains homosexual content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Five, housing policies will prioritise allocation and grants for married couples; and here, marriage means a union of a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Six, library books for children, both physical and digital, should not have content depicting or affirming homosexual unions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Eight and for the complete avoidance of doubt, civil unions and civil partnerships are not recognised in Singapore.

sections.label: PSP position on 377A repeal
sections.summary: Some members set aside personal opinions and did not pursue objection to repealing 377A, so PSP could support the repeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Eventually, recognising that 377A is unenforceable, some members were prepared to put aside their personal opinions and not pursue their objection to the repeal of 377A.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With their compromise, PSP is now able to come to a party position of supporting the repeal of 377A.

sections.label: PSP wants marriage referendum
sections.summary: PSP's position is that the definition of marriage should be decided by a national referendum rather than by Parliament, letting concerned Singaporeans have a say.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP's position is that the definition of marriage should be decided via a national referendum rather than by Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will allow the many Singaporeans who have expressed concerns to have a say in this matter.

sections.label: Gay community and 377A
sections.summary: Ground-up initiatives give the community a safe space, and the gay community sees section 377A as society's judgement, though it is not actively enforced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These ground-up initiatives provide a safe space for their community to come together and support one another, where they can be seen and heard, where they are not treated as invisible and where they will not be judged.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I understand that to the gay community, section 377A, while not actively enforced, is seen as society’s judgement of them – a rejection of their right to exist, criminalises their right to love and be loved in return, and makes them feel like a lesser citizen.

sections.label: Repealing section 377A via two Bills
sections.summary: Two Bills repeal section 377A carefully, addressing concerns about the heterosexual family norm, private consensual sex, and social norms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The two Bills that stand before us today allow us to repeal section 377A in a careful and considered way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Having heard the views from various parties, the two Bills have been drafted with great care, and aim to address their concerns: (a) that the majority of Singaporeans still want the heterosexual family structure as norm; (b) most accept that private consensual sex between men should not be criminalised; and (c) for those who are against the repeal, the main concern is about what the repeal would mean for social norms, and not that they want to criminalise sex between men.

sections.label: 2007 decision to retain 377A
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said in Parliament in 2007 that the Government would retain section 377A but not actively enforce it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said in Parliament in 2007 that the Government had decided to retain section 377A but would not actively enforce the law.

sections.label: Repeal with constitutional marriage amendment
sections.summary: Repealing section 377A brings consistency, and a constitutional amendment clarifies Government power to define and protect marriage as one man and one woman.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Repealing section 377A can bring about consistency in law and practice, and make legislation and law enforcement more consistent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Related to this, just as section 377A may be deemed unconstitutional in Court, Singapore's definition of marriage may face similar challenges, resulting in laws and policies related to marriage being threatened.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: That is why we are proposing to amend the Constitution while repealing section 377A, to clarify that the Government has the power to enact laws to define and protect the institution of marriage, and to prevent the laws and policies related to the institution of marriage on the basis of one man and one woman from being constitutionally challenged.

sections.label: Assurance Package and inflation assistance
sections.summary: 2.9 million Singaporeans receive the Assurance Package next month, and an additional $1.5 billion assistance package was announced last month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For example, 2.9 million Singaporeans will receive the Assurance Package next month to reduce the pressures of cost of living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government has also just announced an additional $1.5 billion assistance package last month to mitigate the pressures of global inflation.

sections.label: Parental concerns on social mores
sections.summary: Some parents may have concerns about repealing section 377A, such as whether it will affect social mores.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Some parents may have concerns about repealing section 377A, such as whether it will affect social mores.

sections.label: Parents' hopes and tolerance of homosexuality
sections.summary: Parents love their children and hope they grow up healthy, find a partner and enjoy family life; we tolerate homosexuality and propose repeal without advocating a lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I also know that parents love their children very much from the bottom of their hearts, hoping that they will grow up in a healthy and harmonious environment, find an ideal partner and have a sense of security in their old age and enjoy family life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We tolerate homosexuality and propose to repeal section 377A and decriminalise homosexuality, but we are not advocating a certain lifestyle or a certain social ethos.

sections.label: Repeal 377A, preserve marriage
sections.summary: The Government proposes to repeal section 377A to align with the law while preserving the institution of marriage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: But we must make the right decision for Singapore, a decision that is responsible to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We propose to repeal section 377A to bring it in line with the law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: At the same time, the institution of marriage should be preserved, not subverted.

sections.label: Advice on 377A court challenge
sections.summary: The Minister for Law and Home Affairs and Attorney-General advised section 377A may be struck down, as the Court of Appeal in Tan Seng Kee held it may breach Article 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Following the latest ruling this year, the Minister for Law and Home Affairs, Mr Shanmugam, and our Attorney-General have advised that there is a high possibility that section 377A will be struck down if it continues to be challenged in future Court cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal in the case of Tan Seng Kee held that the section may not be consistent with Article 12 of the Constitution, which is the right to guarantee equal protection of the law for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: New Article 156(3) protection
sections.summary: New Article 156(3) protects from constitutional challenge laws defining marriage as between a man and a woman and related heterosexual-based laws and policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new Article 156(3) protects from a constitutional challenge the laws defining marriage as a union between a man and a woman and also laws and policies based on a heterosexual definition of marriage.

sections.label: Plans to safeguard marriage institution
sections.summary: A question asks what Government plans exist to promote and safeguard the institution of marriage, including counselling or parenting support for families and parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, may I ask what are the plans of the Government to achieve this stated objective to "promote and safeguard the institution of marriage" and in particular, whether there are any plans to provide families, especially parents, with counselling or parenting support?

sections.label: 2007 position on 377A enforcement
sections.summary: In 2007 Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said the Government will not proactively enforce section 377A, and that has been the position since.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2007, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said that the Government will not proactively enforce section 377A and that has been the position since then.

sections.label: Conscience-based opposition to repeal
sections.summary: A Member says that for reasons of conscience guided by faith and beliefs, they find it difficult to support the repeal of 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Even as I do my best to analyse the issues for different segments of our population and my constituents, for reasons of my own conscience as guided by my own faith and beliefs, I find it difficult to support the repeal of 377A.

sections.label: Support for repeal amendments
sections.summary: Speaker supports the amendments because repealing section 377A without constitutional amendments may worry those with reservations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While I agree that her concerns have some merits – and I look forward to the Government's assurances on these issues – I would still support the amendments for the reason that, as the Government is minded to push through the repeal of section 377A, if the repeal were to proceed without the proposed constitutional amendments, those who have reservations about the repeal may be even more concerned that there will be no other enhancement in law to address their concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would also like to seek the understanding of my constituents and Singaporeans who may not agree with my decision.

sections.label: Laws strengthening marriage and families
sections.summary: Laws and institutions must help strengthen a culture where husbands and wives prioritise strong families, and early interventions can improve social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While it has to be acknowledged that there are major challenges that couples will have got to tackle, in order to keep their marriages healthy and to provide the best environment to raise their children, our laws and institutions must help to strengthen the culture, where husbands and wives give priority to building strong families, even when couples are economically disadvantaged, public policy, through early interventions in their children's lives can help to improve social mobility.

sections.label: Redefining family leaves uncharted waters
sections.summary: Departing from the norm of family as marriage between a man and a woman leaves uncharted waters and involves sequential steps.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Departing from this norm, or what constitutes a family, I believe, leaves us in uncharted waters.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also affirms: "the family as the cornerstone of our social fabric, and marriage between a man and a woman." A strategy to redefine what constitutes a family from what the Government has reaffirmed as marriage between a man and woman and their parenthood, involves taking sequential steps to progressively bring about change.

sections.label: Keeping law to preserve family structure
sections.summary: Speaker believes not repealing the law preserves the family form of marriage between a man and a woman as cornerstone.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These legislative changes make the definition of the institution of marriage, both contingent and subject to change.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe that not repealing the law acts to bolster the achieving of the aims of the Government to keep the family form out of a marriage between a man and a woman, as a cornerstone of our social fabric for as long as possible, in the face of the many challenges to such an understanding of the family as the unit that forms the basic structure of society.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe that keeping the current law serves to provide an important marker to preserve the present structure of the family and its supporting institution.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe that it is best not to repeal the law.

sections.label: NTUC on fair treatment and non-participation
sections.summary: NTUC says employees should be treated fairly on merit and not forced to join diversity events or face discrimination for non-participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: NTUC believes that all employees should be treated fairly based on merit and should not be discriminated based on any non-job-related characteristics, which may include faith or identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: NTUC calls on companies organising programmes or events for employees in support of diversity and inclusion causes to ensure that employees who choose not to attend such activities for non-job-related requirements are not forced to join or made to feel discriminated for not participating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Non-participation must not affect the career progression of employees.

sections.label: Support for Bill and inclusivity
sections.summary: Speaker supports the Bill in view of inclusivity in a diverse community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Having listed my concerns earlier, I support the Bill in view of inclusivity in a diverse community.

sections.label: 377A as moral marker
sections.summary: The speaker says the middle ground is strong and asks whether repealing 377A would lead to views being cancelled or treated as hatred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Despite our worst fears, in my humble opinion, Sir, the middle ground on this issue is strong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And Mr Speaker, Sir, given that no one is calling for the active enforcement of 377A in this debate, as we move on to unpack the issues, we must hold fast in our hearts to that realisation, because it is the truth that unifies and heals and strengthens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is at stake is the existence of 377A on our statute books as a moral marker, as a symbolic marker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And as I said in my recent speech on national symbols, the debate is not less important for that reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And that is the concern that if 377A is repealed and that moral marker is no longer, will those who do not view LGBTQ+ relationships as being consonant with their own personal values, will such people be cancelled from expressing their view, will the expression of their views, say religious views for example, be considered to be acts of hatred and discrimination?

sections.label: Law and private behaviour
sections.summary: The speaker's view is that the law may intervene in private behaviour with public consequences, even when consensual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My own view is that there is a public sphere where the law has the right to intervene in private behaviour that has public consequences, even when that private behaviour is consensual on the part of all participants.

sections.label: Debate on 377A marker
sections.summary: The speaker recalls that the debate is about keeping or removing 377A as a symbolic marker, not about actively enforcing it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, some have made points about public health, some about our ability to reproduce as a nation, some about the undesirability of importing liberal values from the west and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, let us recall, this is a debate about keeping or throwing out 377A as a symbolic marker, not about actively enforcing it, where there is no disagreement.

sections.label: Non-enforcement stance reversible
sections.summary: The Government and Attorney General will not proactively enforce 377A, but a future government or AGC could reverse this stance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: No doubt, the current Government has declared that it will not proactively enforce 377A and the Attorney General has said that the Public Prosecutor will hew to this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But this leaves the door open to a future government and Attorney-General's Chamber (AGC) to reverse this stance.

sections.label: Keeping unenforced law criticised
sections.summary: The speaker says keeping a law with serious impact on many Singaporeans because it is an unenforced marker is not good lawmaking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To keep a law that has a serious impact on the lives of many Singaporeans on the basis that it is a marker that will not be enforced by the current Government is not in my opinion, how we should go about making good laws.

sections.label: Respectful rational public discussion
sections.summary: The speaker says Singaporeans should cultivate respectful, rational talk to decide matters, politics and laws, and agree to disagree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Surely, the answer to that question is to cultivate the ability for Singaporeans to talk to each other respectfully and rationally, to decide on important matters that way, to decide our politics that way, to decide our laws that way, to agree to disagree that way, when perfect consensus cannot be forged – as it cannot on a range of issues, not only on section 377A.

sections.label: Respectful disagreement in national discourse
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether national discourse can move towards respectfully agreeing to disagree while defending the political centre against hatred, bigotry and violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These views are very deeply rooted and passionate on both sides.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But can we succeed in moving the needle towards this ideal, so that more and more and more of our national discourse gradually becomes like this, not in a straight line, maybe a zig-zag, messy line, but moving more and more towards a dominant paradigm that says that we can respectfully agree to disagree and tomorrow we will still be fellow Singaporeans, still be brothers and sisters, still defend the political centre and push those spewing hatred, bigotry and violence to the fringes?

sections.label: Workers' Party colleagues on 377A
sections.summary: The speaker says he is optimistic Singapore can do it, because Workers' Party colleagues debated, learnt from one another and decided democratically on 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From my discussions I have had with my Workers' Party colleagues who have expressed or will express different views from mine in Parliament today on 377A, I would like to say that I am optimistic that Singapore can do it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Because my colleagues and I strive together for a democratic society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And on this issue, we debated, discussed, learnt from one another, agreed to disagree with respect and humility and affection, and we decided democratically.

sections.label: Lee's 377A repeal announcement
sections.summary: The speaker recalls Prime Minister Lee saying "It works, do not disturb it" and being taken aback by the 2022 National Day Rally repeal announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee said, "It works, do not disturb it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It works, do not disturb it." Thus, 15 years later, when Prime Minister Lee made his announcement during the National Day Rally in August that the Government intends to repeal section 377A of the Penal Code, I was taken aback.

sections.label: Repeal and marriage laws
sections.summary: The passage states repeal reinforces that Parliament decides marriage laws, that these cannot be challenged as discriminatory under Part 4, and gives assurance of no drastic shift in norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Will the repeal of section 377A mean that the family is no longer the basic building block of society?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It reinforces the Government's stand that the definition of marriage and laws to protect, safeguard, support, foster and promote the institution of marriage should be for Parliament to decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And that Parliament's power to make such laws on marriage cannot be challenged under Part 4 of the Constitution to be discriminatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It gives assurance to many Singaporeans that the repeal of section 377A will not lead to a drastic shift in societal norms.

sections.label: Protections and pro-family policies
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to ensure no organisation, company or school compels participation in gay community projects, to legislate against hate messages, and to keep policies pro-family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And likewise, for students studying in international schools, they are asked to take part in gay-themed projects as if it was part and parcel of the school curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to look into this and ensure that no organisation, company or school in Singapore can compel their staff or students to participate in gay community projects if they do not subscribe to the same values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I submit that every organisation, company or school must have the scope to allow their employees or students to subscribe to different views on sexuality without being discriminated or having to receive hate mail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I also urge the Government to consider legislation to make it an offence for anyone to put out hate messages or derogatory comments just purely to intimidate others into keeping silent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And this law should apply equally to those who are anti-gay and those gays who seek to bully others into silent submission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Even as we move to repeal section 377A, I hope that the Government will also make clear its stand that our policies on sexuality education in schools, our content guidelines for publications, for video games and various type of media will remain pro-family, that we will not see a proliferation of materials, video games or media advertisements promoting the gay lifestyle, that we will not have laws that allow individuals to remove their gender in their NRIC or passport and that the Government will remind all organisations, companies and even embassies operating in Singapore that we are still a society that values family as the basic building block of society.

sections.label: Concerns over repealing 377A
sections.summary: The passage lists concerns that repeal removes a societal marker, causes a domino effect towards normalisation of homosexuality, and makes expressing beliefs harder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, there are concerns that the repeal of section 377A will remove an important societal marker and open the door to an erosion of traditional values in our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, some are worried that after this law is repealed, there will be a domino effect on other regulations and policies, leading towards a normalisation of homosexuality in our society – from changes to sexuality education in schools to more liberal media portrayals and eventually, the legalisation of same-sex marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, many, especially those from the younger age groups, are concerned that as the societal narrative shifts, they will find it harder to freely express their own beliefs without being labelled as homophobic.

sections.label: Public Prosecutor on section 377A
sections.summary: The Public Prosecutor's position is that prosecuting two consenting adults in private under section 377A, absent other factors, would not be in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He added that the Public Prosecutor has taken the position that prosecution of two consenting adults in a private place under section 377A, absent other factors, would not be in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This assurance was strengthened when the Court of Appeal wrote in February 2022 that section 377A is "unenforceable in its entirety" unless and until the Public Prosecutor of the day provides clear notice that he intends to reassert his right to enforce section 377A proactively by way of prosecution and will no longer abide by the representations made by Attorney-General Lucien Wong in 2018.

sections.label: Conscience vote on repeal
sections.summary: The member's conscience does not allow voting for repeal of section 377A, and the lifted whip permits Workers' Party MPs to cast conscience votes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The final reason for the vote I am about to cast is that my conscience does not allow me to vote in favour of a repeal of section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am grateful to the Leader of the Opposition for lifting the whip on Workers' Party Members of Parliament for a vote on both these Bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This permits Workers' Party Members of Parliament to cast "conscience votes" on these Bills.

sections.label: Faith, conscience and voters
sections.summary: Members' faith and conscience may differ on the country's best interests, and a constituent said he would not vote for the member because of this stand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, what one member, informed by their faith and conscience, believes to be in the best interests of the country in some issues may differ from what another member believes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have been told in my face by a constituent that he will not vote for me in the future because of my stand on this issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I accept the importance that many Singaporeans place on their elected Members of Parliament's positions on these Bills to the extent that it will be a factor in their decisions at the polls.

sections.label: Repeal for inclusive Singapore
sections.summary: Repealing section 377A is the right thing to do to ensure Singapore is an inclusive and diverse place for everyone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The repeal of section 377A is the right thing to do if we are to ensure that Singapore is an inclusive and diverse place to live in and for everyone to be a part of.

sections.label: Welcoming marriage constitutional amendment
sections.summary: The member welcomes the reinforcement of the institution of marriage by the amendment in the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: On the reinforcement of the institution of marriage by the amendment in the Constitution, I welcome it.

sections.label: Protecting current marriage definition
sections.summary: The constitutional amendment will protect the current definition of marriage while other national policies on marriage and family remain unchanged.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The process can take hundreds and thousands of years, decades or just a few years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This constitutional amendment will protect the current definition of marriage while other national policies relating to marriage and family will remain unchanged.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: The speaker says controlling gay people's private lives is selfish and supports repealing section 377A to decriminalise gay sex.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: If we enjoy their novels, lyrics and songs they have written and like their movies and stage productions, but on the other hand, we want to control their private lives by law and not allow them to be intimate with their loved ones, are we not too selfish and overboard?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code to decriminalise gay sex.

sections.label: LGBTQ+ community and future change
sections.summary: The speaker says the LGBTQ+ community should not be discriminated against, but public perception changes take time and action follows ripe sentiments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: It is difficult to predict how society will change in the future and how our children and grandchildren decide to govern themselves then.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: It is important that the members of Singapore's LGBTQ+ community are not discriminated against for choosing how they want to live their lives and for who they love.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, changes in public perception will take time and we will act accordingly if and when these sentiments are ripe.

sections.label: Tolerant inclusive Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker supports repealing section 377A and amending the Constitution to protect the prevailing definition of marriage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Today, we are taking a step towards a more tolerant and inclusive Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Let us continue to keep the love for everyone in Singapore's society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and Environment and Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: I support the repeal of section 377A and the amendment of the Constitution to protect the prevailing definition of marriage.

sections.label: Uneasy 2007 political compromise
sections.summary: The speaker says the 2007 compromise was uneasy as court challenges risked striking down 377A, and non-enforcement made it redundant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This has held true for many years, in particular the last 15, following the political compromise of 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But it was an uneasy compromise as each constitutional challenge risked it being struck down by the Courts rather than legislated by Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: By not proactively enforcing 377A also in essence made it redundant as a law.

sections.label: Poll on same-sex marriage
sections.summary: The speaker cites a poll finding a majority of Singaporeans oppose same-sex marriage, with 66% agreeing to enshrine marriage as between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet, earlier this year, a poll did find that a majority of Singaporeans oppose same-sex marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Some 66% also agree with a proposal to perhaps consider enshrining marriage as “only between a man and a woman".

sections.label: Constitutional amendment and marriage liberty
sections.summary: The speaker supports the constitutional amendment but would have preferred enshrining heterosexual marriage as a fundamental liberty in the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Because in a democracy, it is important that the viewpoints of all citizens can be heard and taken into consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I do support the constitutional amendment, but as some would be aware, I would have preferred to push for heterosexual marriage to be enshrined or codified as a fundamental liberty in our Constitution.

sections.label: Marriage definition court challenge
sections.summary: Article 156 states the Government cannot be challenged in Court over the definition of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The amendment as it stands in Article 156, spells out that the Government cannot be challenged in Court over the definition of marriage.

sections.label: Protections for beliefs on marriage
sections.summary: It asks what protections free businesses and religious organisations from legal challenges over teachings and beliefs on marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
