sentences.text: Singaporeans must feel free and safe to practise their beliefs without fear of backlash, as long as their own actions do not cause harm or danger to others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, what protections are there to ensure that businesses and other institutions, such as religious organisations, are freed from legal challenges regarding teachings and beliefs on marriage?

sections.label: Support for repeal with amendment
sections.summary: The speaker supports repealing 377A with the passage of the constitutional amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As such, I am prepared to support the repeal of 377A with the passage of the constitutional amendment.

sections.label: Traditional family and children's support
sections.summary: The speaker believes in the traditional family as an ideal, but says all children deserve fullest support regardless of family circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: That is why one of the things which I am proudest about was to have been one of the people behind the founding of Dads for Life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, yes, I do believe, absolutely, with no apology and with no reservations, in the traditional family form as an ideal – one man, one woman, committed to each other to bring up their children in the context of a stable marriage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Having said that, we also need to acknowledge that not everyone will be so blessed and enjoy such a simple, straightforward life, that sometimes life does not go according to plan, and that all children, regardless of family circumstances, deserve our fullest support.

sections.label: Falling short and 377A debate
sections.summary: The speaker apologises to gay friends for falling short, and says section 377A symbolises two paradoxical imperatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Yet, I think, if many of us think back to our school days, I think we all fell short.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I will confess to having fallen short and for that, I apologise to my gay friends.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, this debate on section 377A of the Penal Code – section 377A has come to symbolise simultaneously two paradoxical imperatives.

sections.label: Repeal to avoid court risk
sections.summary: The speaker accepts 377A is at legal risk, supports repeal to avoid a Court confrontation, and supports the constitutional amendment on marriage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam has explained – and I accept his explanation – that section 377A is at significant legal risk of being struck down.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The amendments proposed today to repeal 377A, I believe, helps us avoid that abrupt and potentially disruptive confrontation in a Court of law with a binary outcome and perhaps unpredictable and sometimes uncontrollable social and political consequences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, I agree with him and I support the repeal of 377A in that context.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But I also support the amendment to the Constitution that makes it clear that the question of marriage will be decided here in this House.

sections.label: Traditional family and parenthood support
sections.summary: Policies and programmes will unambitiously support the traditional family and parenthood, including adoption rights, housing priority, Baby Bonuses and reproductive therapy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In practice, what that means is policies and programmes that will unambitiously support the traditional family and parenthood, including adoption rights, housing priority, Baby Bonuses and reproductive therapy.

sections.label: Repeal and marriage definition decision
sections.summary: The decision to repeal section 377A and amend the Constitution to protect the marriage definition followed extensive engagements and careful consideration of feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   The decision to repeal section 377A of the Penal Code and amend the Constitution to protect the definition of marriage and the laws and policies that are based on it from legal challenges was not made overnight.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It is the result of extensive engagements with stakeholders and careful consideration of the feedback received both before Prime Minister's announcement at this year's National Day Rally and in the ensuing months.

sections.label: Evolving societal mindsets and attitudes
sections.summary: Since the 2007 Parliament debate, society's mindset and attitudes have evolved and are expected to continue evolving in coming decades.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Ever since this issue was last debated in Parliament in 2007, society's mindset and attitudes have evolved, and we can expect it to continue evolving in the coming decades.

sections.label: Government approach combining beliefs and needs
sections.summary: The Government's approach combines religious beliefs, family values and traditional communities with the needs of Singapore's multi-religious and multicultural society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health and Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The approach taken by the Government combines religious beliefs, family values and traditional communities with the needs of Singapore’s multi-religious and multicultural society.

sections.label: PM on shifted social attitudes
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said in the 2022 National Day Rally that social attitudes towards gay people have shifted appreciably and repeal will bring the law into line with current social mores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister had said in the 2022 National Day Rally, social attitudes towards gay people have "shifted appreciably" and the repeal of the provision will "bring the law into line with current social mores".

sections.label: Avoiding stigmatisation and discrimination
sections.summary: While repealing section 377A is a major step in the right direction, public policies affecting gay Singaporeans should not result in stigmatisation and discrimination on a practical level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the repeal of section 377A is a major step in the right direction, we should also ensure that public policies that affect gay Singaporeans in their everyday lives do not result in any form of stigmatisation and discrimination on a practical level.

sections.label: Adaptive stance on public policies
sections.summary: The speaker says it may be pragmatic for the Government to adopt an adaptive stance towards public policies, including those affecting gay Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It may not be prudent to adopt an immutable stance towards any public policies, as we may find ourselves out of sync with the realities on the ground in time to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, it may be pragmatic for the Government to always adopt an adaptive stance towards public policies, including policies affecting gay Singaporeans.

sections.label: Support for repealing section 377A
sections.summary: The speaker states support for the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With that, I support the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code.

sections.label: Protecting marriage definition from challenges
sections.summary: New Article 156 subsections (3) and (4) seek to protect the definition of marriage in laws from constitutional challenges, with PAP's commitment that it will not change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The new Article 156 subsection (3) and subsection (4), seek to protect the definition of marriage in such laws like the Women's Charter, the Administration of Muslim Law Act and laws that confer rights and benefits on or in relation to persons married under those enactment, from constitutional challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Pro-family policies of the Government, for example, in regard to housing, education and media standards will therefore also be protected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But the anxiety is if this would make it easy for change as it will only require a simple majority to amend the definition of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I have received feedback from some asking that the definition of marriage be directly in the Constitution so as to require a two-thirds majority and not just a simple majority to affect such a radical redefinition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To give further reassurance, Deputy Prime Minister Wong has given PAP's commitment that the definition of marriage as that of the union between a man and a woman, will not change under the watch of the current leadership of Prime Minister Lee and if the PAP Government were to win the next General Election, it will not change under his watch.

sections.label: Concern about bullying and cancel culture
sections.summary: The speaker says bullying and a cancel culture are an area of concern that must be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: From the reactions and feedback shared, an area that is of concern and we must address is that of bullying and a cancel culture.

sections.label: No labelling, discrimination or bullying
sections.summary: The speaker says no persons should be labelled, discriminated or bullied, and agencies are looking at ways to ensure discrimination is not tolerated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What we cannot allow is for any persons, regardless of which side they stand on, to be labelled, discriminated or bullied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam and Minister of State Sun Xueling have shared that the agencies are looking at ways to ensure that discrimination is not tolerated.

sections.label: Support for Penal Code and Constitution amendments
sections.summary: The speaker says how we act will determine Singapore, and supports the Penal Code amendment and the amendment to the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I do believe that while the amendments strive to provide the legislation to preserve and protect our social norms, how we act will determine the Singapore we have today and in the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I support the Penal Code amendment as well as the amendment to the Constitution.

sections.label: Repeal 377A and marriage protection
sections.summary: The speaker says repealing 377A must come with strong constitutional protection of the recognised legal union between a man and woman.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: By not having it as mainstream, we can at best defer the exposure of the young ones to a later stage when they are more mature to differentiate or make sound decisions independently.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Thus, I firmly believe that to repeal 377A, it must be done on the grounds where the recognised legal union between a man and woman is also strongly protected by definition within the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: While we can now take reference of this in the form of Article 156 if it is passed, we must ensure that the Government stands by this firmly as we consider any future amendments to the legislation or even the repeals.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Today, HDB public housing can be purchased or rented by those who have a family nucleus.

sections.label: Family nucleus application fairness
sections.summary: Applications are limited by conditions or considered case-by-case, raising fairness questions if the family nucleus definition for married couples changes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: But their applications are currently either limited by conditions or considered on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, this brings about the question of fairness if the definition of family nucleus for a married couple changes.

sections.label: Pro-people, pro-Singapore principles
sections.summary: The speaker says they are pro-people and pro-Singapore, principles behind speaking in support of the Bill and repeal of 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My reply was, to that person who asked me, and is, that I am “pro-people” and “pro-Singapore”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These are two principles that I have always strongly believed in and it is why I am speaking today in support of this Bill and the subsequent repeal of 377A.

sections.label: Private sex should not be criminal
sections.summary: The speaker says two men having sex in private is a personal matter and should not be regarded as criminal, so repealing 377A is right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Two men having sex in private is precisely that, a private and, in my opinion, a personal matter, and it should not be something that is regarded as criminal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, I believe that repealing 377A is, thus, the right thing to do because it is the right thing to do.

sections.label: Educator training and societal conversations
sections.summary: The speaker suggests training educators to handle identity issues and hopes society continues respectful conversations, while worrying fault lines are being drawn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There could also be instances when students themselves are exploring their own identity and having trained educators who could help them in this journey of discovery would be important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I feel it would be good if the Government could consider how educators could be trained to handle these issues and other related topics that might emerge from this debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps these parts are parts of our community that we have not always heard, engaged or connected with, and who are somehow feeling that they are like a discarded scrap of cloth, rather than part of a beautiful and wonderful quilt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But I believe that what continues to connect us, what will help mend the tears and strengthen the fabric in our quilt, will be the strong threads that start with conversation, dialogue and understanding, and all done with respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, while this debate might be settled in the House over the next couple of days, I hope that the different groups in our society will continue to have important and relevant conversations and treat one another with dignity and respect, so that we can, indeed, work towards a Singapore that emerges stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Minister Masagos, would you like to move the Motion for Exempted Business?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I would like to express my worry that fault lines are being drawn in our society as a result of the views of various groups in our society occupying the centrestage on this issue.

sections.label: Society cannot afford polarisation
sections.summary: The speaker says society cannot afford to be polarised by this issue, given the many challenges facing families, communities and the nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our society cannot afford to be polarised by this issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We have already so many challenges facing us, as families, as communities and as a nation.

sections.label: Combating social and income inequality
sections.summary: The speaker calls for combating social and income inequality so no Singaporean is left behind, and for society to work together to bridge differences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to combat social and income inequality and strive to make sure that no Singaporean is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that cool heads will prevail and we can all take a step back and understand one another's positions and work together as a society to bridge any differences.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee announced Singapore will repeal section 377A and amend the Constitution to protect the definition of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At the National Day Rally, Prime Minister Lee's announcement that Singapore will repeal section 377A of the Penal Code and amend the Constitution to protect the definition of marriage reflects the common agreement that many believe our gay citizens have a place in society and should not be treated as criminals.

sections.label: Risk of section 377A struck down
sections.summary: The speaker says the significant risk of section 377A being struck down for breaching equal protection must also be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition to shifting societal values, we have to also consider the "significant risk" of section 377A being struck down in a Court of law on the grounds that it breaches the provisions of "equal protection" in our Constitution, as discussed extensively by Minister Shanmugam earlier.

sections.label: Tan Seng Kee court case
sections.summary: In Tan Seng Kee vs Attorney-General, the Attorney-General's Chambers found a significant risk section 377A could be rejected in Court for violating equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, in the case of Tan Seng Kee vs Attorney-General, the Attorney-General's Chambers found that there is a significant risk that section 377A could be rejected in Court, because it violates the provision for equality in our Constitution.

sections.label: PAP family and marriage policies
sections.summary: The speaker was pleased Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong assured PAP will uphold family-first policies and marriage as between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, I was pleased that Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong gave his assurance that PAP will continue to uphold policies that puts the family first and will continue to ensure that marriage will be defined as between a man and a woman.

sections.label: Repeal with marriage definition protected
sections.summary: The speaker says they want to repeal section 377A while protecting the prevailing definition of marriage, with Parliament defining marriage based on prevailing Singaporean values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While we would like to repeal section 377A, we would also like to protect the prevailing definition of marriage while still allowing recourse in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: By ensuring that the definition of marriage is dependent on Parliament, and Parliament will define marriage based on the prevailing values and views of the Singaporean society at any given point of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At this juncture, I wish to thank Prime Minister Lee and Deputy Minister Lawrence Wong for the clear assurance that "the PAP Government will continue to uphold our family-centred policies and is fully committed to them and will continue to uphold marriage as defined between man and woman." In this way, even if one does not agree with the repeal of section 377A, at least the definition of marriage is preserved, for the time being, in our Constitution.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: The speaker supports repealing section 377A and the constitutional amendment giving Parliament power over marriage laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the points considered earlier, Mr Speaker, Sir, I do support the repeal in the Penal Code and the amendments to the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Singapore Government has decided to finally repeal section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe section 377A is no longer relevant in contemporary Singaporean society and I agree with its repeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to state my support for the inclusion of Article 156 of the Constitution, which clarifies that the power to make laws to do with the institution of marriage rightly rests with this very Parliament and for Parliament to protect the prevailing definition of marriage.

sections.label: Policy review for unmarried people
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether PMO can coordinate a whole-of-Government policy review that actively considers unmarried people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, can PMO consider coordinating a policy review across the whole-of-Government and ensure that those who are not married are actively considered as part of the policy-making process?

sections.label: Children and non-traditional peers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether enough is done so children do not treat peers outside the traditional family unit differently or derisively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Are we doing enough to ensure that our children understand that even though their peers may not fit into the definition of a traditional family unit, either because of their home situation or their personal realities, that these peers should not be treated differently or, worse, derisively?

sections.label: Youths want 377A gone
sections.summary: The speaker says most youths want section 377A gone because it suggests some Singaporeans are less than others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Most of our youths want section 377A gone, because it suggests that some Singaporeans are less than others.

sections.label: Youths support proposed amendments
sections.summary: The speaker says youths empathise with differing views and so most will support the amendments proposed today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And because our youths can empathise with differing viewpoints, our youths now have a deeper sense of understanding of how our more traditional Singaporeans feel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, I believe that most of our youths will support the amendments proposed today.

sections.label: Support for proposed amendments
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for legislation against cancel culture and supports the amendments as consensus-building that refreshes the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: At that age, our youths are at the discovery stage in their lives and our educators have a lot less influence over their students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope we can consider legislations, moving forward, to prevent the "cancel culture" from taking root in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I stand in support of the proposed amendments because they are the result of a painstaking consensus building effort, thereby cementing our common ground into law, and also because they refresh our social compact on gender and marriage for the years ahead, thereby addressing the very reasonable concerns of more traditional Singaporeans, and because it helps us move Singapore forward.

sections.label: 377A repeal and personal convictions
sections.summary: The speaker says the repeal of section 377A and proposed constitutional amendments involve an intractable divide and personal convictions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a matter such as the repeal of section 377A and the attendant proposed constitutional amendments, however, it would appear that there is not only an intractable divide between the different interests that we represent, but our own personal convictions may play a role in the choices we are forced in make.

sections.label: Repeal as trade-off
sections.summary: The speaker describes the repeal decision as a trade-off between removing a threat of imprisonment and concern over undermining marriage.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The repeal decision is thus a trade-off between the removal of a tangible, actual threat of imprisonment, versus a perceived, potential concern over how repeal would undermine marriage.

sections.label: Sexual relations between men offence
sections.summary: The speaker states that sexual relations between men remains, on the books, an arrestable offence.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even so, sexual relations between men remains, on the books, an arrestable offence.

sections.label: Law declaring individuals criminals
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether individuals can feel accepted when Singaporean law declares them to be criminals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can we expect such individuals to truly feel that they are accepted as a part of Singaporean society, when Singaporean law declares them to be criminals?

sections.label: Support for repealing 377A
sections.summary: The speaker states that for these reasons, they support the repeal of the discriminatory law that is 377A.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For these reasons, I support the repeal of the discriminatory law that is 377A.

sections.label: Constitutional change and judicial activism
sections.summary: The speaker says altering the Constitution is not merely political expediency but echoes what society believes, citing Prime Minister Lee on judicial activism.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just as important, threats to these identities affect their behaviours and their welfare.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that I do not see a decision to alter the Constitution as essentially a compromise for merely the sake of political expediency, necessary for the repeal of 377A.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Rather, it is the manner by which the state will echo what society, as a whole, believes in.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee had explained in his National Day Rally speech that challenges via the judicial system were becoming more insistent, and that we did not wish to go down the dangerous road of judicial activism.

sections.label: Marriage definition constitutional amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments only let the legislature define marriage, and the speaker opposes hardcoding a heterosexual definition into the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Keen observers will nevertheless note that the constitutional amendments that were proposed, however, merely refer to how the legislature may define marriage, leaving the specific definition indeterminate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is where I depart from those who would go further, those who are asking for a heterosexual definition of marriage be hardcoded into the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In contrast to the more fundamental notion of the institution of marriage, its definition does not strike me as an unwavering principle that belongs to a constitution.

sections.label: Pledge and marriage values
sections.summary: The speaker says the pledge to build a democratic society calls for affirming common values like marriage, so will vote yes to both amendments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But at the same time, our commitment to – also in our pledge – "build a democratic society" calls on us to affirm our common values, such as marriage, that make us one united people.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That is why I will vote yes to both of these amendments today.

sections.label: Opposing discriminatory law
sections.summary: The speaker says we must not discriminate against fellow citizens and therefore votes in support of repeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must above all, work to not discriminate against our fellow citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is this principle that moves me to vote in support of repeal today.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I do not believe that we should have a law in the books that is plainly and obviously discriminatory.

sections.label: Repeal and anti-discrimination legislation
sections.summary: The speaker says not repealing section 377A would conflict with Singapore's steps towards a fairer society and planned anti-discrimination legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Not repealing section 377A today would be at odds with steps that Singapore is taking to be a fairer and more equitable society for all and will go against the principles behind the Government's welcome announcement that we will finally legislate against discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Many in this House have already mentioned the Government's announcement to introduce anti-discrimination legislation and I believe the repeal of section 377A plays its part in our move towards a more inclusive society.

sections.label: Amendments shield marriage laws from review
sections.summary: The speaker says Articles 156(3)(b) and (4) prevent laws and policies on the heterosexual definition of marriage from being challenged in Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, from a legal perspective, the proposed amendments carve out an area of legislative decision-making and functionally shields it from judicial review.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Specifically, the proposed Articles 156(3)(b) and (4) prevent laws and policies relating to the heterosexual definition of marriage from being challenged in Court on the basis of the fundamental liberties provisions in the Constitution.

sections.label: Article 156 shields legislation from review
sections.summary: The speaker says Article 156 functionally shields legislation from being tested against Part 4 fundamental liberties protections.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Article 156, while not an ouster clause in the traditional sense, functionally shields legislation from being tested against the protection of fundamental liberties under Part 4 of the Constitution.

sections.label: Abstaining over judicial oversight carve-out
sections.summary: The speaker abstains from the proposed constitutional amendments due to concerns about a carve-out from judicial oversight, despite understanding why Article 156 was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Although I understand and appreciate why the Government has introduced the new Article 156, I find that I must abstain from the amendments proposed to the Constitution due to my concerns relating to the carve-out from judicial oversight.

sections.label: Empathy for LGBTI Singaporeans after repeal
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Singaporeans empathise with LGBTI members and that both sides avoid imposing views, saying life will go on after section 377A is repealed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, to some of our fellow Singaporeans, every moment of their lives is affected by it.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We do not have to condone it nor encourage it, but I hope we can find it within ourselves to try to empathise with them, even just a little bit – that we can find it within ourselves to be able to live and hope and pray that the LGBTI members of our community are able to live without discrimination and fear of being ostracised.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Conversely, those who support the repeal of section 377A or even feel that we should go further should also not attempt to bludgeon their views upon those who are deeply uncomfortable with it and instead try to understand the reasons behind why they feel this way.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After section 377A is repealed, life will go on.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Love and hope can still triumph over anger and mistrust, and we will still open our doors and hearts to our neighbours in the community who need an extra helping hand – like the countless stories of neighbourhood group chats stepping in during the pandemic, the students of our Sengkang schools who came together to make gift cards to show their appreciation for our healthcare heroes in our healthcare facilities and their vaccination centres.

sections.label: Doctor treating all patients equally
sections.summary: As a doctor, the speaker will treat all patients equally regardless of race, language, religion, sexual preferences or gender identity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a doctor, I will treat all patients who come before me equally, regardless of race, language or religion, and – I add – sexual preferences or gender identity.

sections.label: Applauding LGBTQ advocates, decriminalisation change
sections.summary: The speaker applauds LGBTQ rights advocates' commitment and bravery and is glad the homosexual male will be decriminalised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For those who have advocated actively for LGBTQ rights, I applaud their steadfast commitment and bravery.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad that one key change will be achieved – the decriminalisation of the homosexual male.

sections.label: Reviewing school sex education
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOE to review the sex education component to ensure it is based on science and facts, with controversial opinions stated as such.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In schools, I urge MOE to review the sex education component to ensure that it is based on science and facts, while controversial opinions and trends are clearly stated as such.

sections.label: Divisiveness of discussing LGBT rights
sections.summary: The speaker is deeply aware of how divisive discussing LGBT rights is and how society may become fragmented.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We react with anger when we are hurt.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am deeply aware of how divisive discussing LGBTs rights is and how society may become fragmented.

sections.label: Decriminalisation and marriage protection together
sections.summary: Parliament deliberately acts to decriminalise gay sex and protect marriage at the same time, as a balanced arrangement society can accept.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Legislatively, there is no obligation or inevitability that as we decriminalise gay sex, we will also protect the institution of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is a deliberate act of Parliament, a carefully considered and balanced decision and move, to do both at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And we do it, because we know that taken together, this set of arrangements would be one that our society, as a whole, can probably accept, and it can point a way forward for all of us.

sections.label: Survey on 377A and marriage
sections.summary: Sixty-eight percent view repealing 377A positively, while an almost equal proportion wishes to uphold marriage as between one man and one woman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Sixty-eight percent view the repeal of 377A positively and at the same time, an almost equal proportion wishes to uphold the current definition of marriage between one man and one woman.

sections.label: Private sexual life not criminal
sections.summary: The speaker says private sexual life should not be a criminal offence and supports repealing section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think we can also agree that we have no reason to regard their sexual life in private as a criminal offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I therefore support the repeal of section 377A.

sections.label: Constitutional protection for marriage definition
sections.summary: Concerns about same-sex marriage lead the Government to propose amending the Constitution to protect the current definition of marriage alongside repealing 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: If the next step after repealing section 377A is to recognise and allow same-sex marriage, what will happen to the norms and core values of our society?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: These concerns are fundamental and important, and it is precisely because of this that together with repealing section 377A, the Government is also proposing to amend the Constitution to protect the current definition of marriage.

sections.label: PAP did not lift Whip
sections.summary: The PAP did not lift the Whip, enabling the ruling party to carry out policy smoothly, which the speaker calls a victory for democracy and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The key to a successful policy is its smooth implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This time, the PAP did not lift the Whip.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The ruling party’s job is to rule and enable policies to be carried out smoothly, and the ruling party has achieved this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is a victory for our democratic system and for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Cheng San-Seletar residents' views
sections.summary: Residents told the speaker they do not believe intimacy between two consenting men should be a crime but wish to preserve the family definition and institution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Over the past few months, a number of my residence in Cheng San-Seletar have written to me or even come down to my Meet-the-People Sessions to express that, while they do not believe that acts of intimacy between two consenting men should be a crime, they sincerely wish to preserve the definition and institution of family.

sections.label: Public Prosecutor non-prosecution affirmation
sections.summary: Attorney-General Lucien Wong affirmed the Public Prosecutor would not prosecute two consenting men for private sex, giving legal significance to the 2007 political compromise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Later in 2018, Attorney-General Lucien Wong affirmed the Public Prosecutor would not prosecute two consenting men for having sex in private, giving legal significance to the political compromise struck in 2007.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: The speaker supports repealing section 377A, calling it a dead letter law, and understands Article 156 as balancing protection of the existing marriage definition with space for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For most, the disagreement lies solely in if it should be repealed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, we must ask ourselves, objectively, 15 years on, should we accept the legal untidiness and ambiguity, given that over the last 15 years, there has been little public interest in seeing section 377A enforced?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From a legal perspective, it is not quite tenable for us to keep this dead letter law and I support the repeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For this reason, I can understand the intention of the introduction of Article 156 to the Constitution as part of a package of amendments which strives to reflect a balance – protecting the existing definition of marriage from constitutional challenges per the majority views today while leaving space for future generations to make their own decisions based on the contexts of their time.

sections.label: Hope for family institution protection
sections.summary: Many people in conversations expressed hope that the family institution will be protected in addition to the repeal of Section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In our conversations, many have expressed hope that the family institution will be protected, in addition to the repeal of Section 377A.

sections.label: Compassion and individual dignity
sections.summary: They still believe assistance and social services should be given on the basis of compassion and place importance on individual dignity, regardless of sexuality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, they still believe that any assistance and social services should be given on the basis of compassion and place an importance on the dignity of the individual, regardless of their sexuality.

sections.label: Forward Singapore building societal muscle
sections.summary: As a young nation, Singapore has not had many years to discuss and debate expectations and trade-offs, and the speaker hopes Forward Singapore will build society's muscle to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a young nation, we have not had as many years to discuss and debate or come to a landing of what we expect of each other as well as an understanding of trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am hopeful that efforts such as Forward Singapore will build up the muscle for society to do so, if done well.

sections.label: Risk of section 377A struck down
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee mentioned in his National Day Rally Speech that the Attorney-General and Minister for Law advised there is a real risk of section 377A being struck down in a future Court challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee also mentioned during his National Day Rally Speech that the Attorney-General and the Minister for Law have advised that in a future Court challenge, there is a real risk of section 377A being struck down.

sections.label: Article 156 marriage protection
sections.summary: Article 156(2) lets the Government and public authorities protect, safeguard, support, foster and promote the institution of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At this same juncture, I applaud the Government’s decision of introducing Article 156 into our Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Article 156(2) provides that the Government and public authorities may, in exercising their executive authority, protect, safeguard, support, foster and promote the institution of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is wholly consistent with what most Singaporeans want – which is to maintain the current family and social norms, where marriage is between a man and a woman, and children are brought up in such a family structure.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: The speaker supports repealing section 377A and the constitutional amendment, and calls for equal treatment of every worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, I am sure that the repeal of section 377A will bring some form of relief and comfort to those who have previously felt oppressed by the same – in knowing that our societal norms have shifted and we, as a society, are ready to accept and grant them the space needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my personal view, the Government has arrived at a nice balance – granting homosexuals the space that they need through the repeal, while recognising and upholding the traditional definition of marriage through the constitutional amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In closing, I echo what our Prime Minster said at the National Day Rally that we must maintain the mutual respect and trust that we have painstakingly built up over the years and stay united as one united people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I stand by and support the decision to repeal section 377A as well as amendment to the Constitution because Every Human Matters!

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also call on fellow workers and employers to treat every worker equally regardless of their gender, because Every Worker Matters!

sections.label: Marriage definition in laws
sections.summary: The conventional definition of marriage is set out in the Women's Charter and AMLA, and the amendment protects it from constitutional challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The conventional definition of marriage is set out in our laws – in the Women’s Charter and the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: With the Constitutional amendment, the Government is taking steps to protect the definition of marriage and related laws and policies from constitutional challenges.

sections.label: No same-sex marriage plans
sections.summary: The Government has no plans to change the definition of marriage to include same-sex marriages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Government has no plans to change the definition of marriage to include same-sex marriages.

sections.label: Amendment and 377A repeal approach
sections.summary: The constitutional amendment and repeal of section 377A prevent the Courts from overturning the marriage definition while maintaining unity and social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Taken together, the Constitutional amendment and the repeal of Section 377A reflect the approach that the Government is taking to prevent the definition of marriage from being overturned by the Courts, while doing the right thing and maintaining unity and social cohesion.

sections.label: Mufti on Islamic sexual relations
sections.summary: Mufti clarified that in Islam, only sexual relations between a husband and wife is permitted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Mufti clarified that in Islam, only sexual relations between a husband and wife is permitted.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim leaders preaching homosexuality
sections.summary: Malay/Muslim leaders and asatizah may preach Islamic beliefs on homosexuality, including online, if respectful and not inciting violence or hate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Malay/Muslim community leaders and asatizah can continue to preach freely on Islamic beliefs about homosexuality, including doing so online to engage more youths on the matter, as long as it is done respectfully, and does not cross redlines of inciting violence or hate towards others.

sections.label: Government supports repeal and marriage amendment
sections.summary: The Government supports repealing Section 377A and amending the Constitution to protect marriage, while the community should not ostracise homosexuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In line with what Mufti has stated, although homosexuality is a sin, the community should not reject or ostracise them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We should remain principled and balanced even though we have different views and look at what is best for the society as a whole.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs and National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This is why the Government supports both the repeal of Section 377A and the amendment to the Constitution to protect marriage.

sections.label: Section 377A convictions become spent
sections.summary: Under the Registration of Criminals Act, a section 377A offence is registrable and its criminal record becomes spent after five crime-free years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the Registration of Criminals Act, an offence under section 377A is a registrable crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Any criminal record of a conviction under section 377A will become spent after a crime-free period of five years.

sections.label: Clarify unspent section 377A convictions
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to clarify whether any section 377A convictions remain unspent and how prior convictions will be treated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if there are any individuals with existing records of convictions under section 377A that have not been spent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how these prior convictions will be treated?

sections.label: Support for single unwed parents
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to confirm policies will be reviewed so single unwed parents are adequately supported while marriage is promoted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Indeed, increased support for single parents is one of the main recommendations in the White Paper on Singapore Women's Development, published this year by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have raised recommendations on housing policies to ensure that single unwed parents and their children will have a roof over their heads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have also asked for single unwed parents to receive the Parenthood Tax Rebate, the Working Mothers' Child Relief, and the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is a whole suite of parenthood policies that exclude and discriminate against single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that even as the Government takes steps to define, regulate, protect, safeguard, support, foster and promote the institution of marriage, we will also continue to review our policies to ensure that single unwed parents are adequately supported?

sections.label: Legislative closure on 377A debate
sections.summary: The proposed constitutional amendment and repeal of section 377A will soon bring the debate to a legislative closure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has listened and the proposed amendment to the Constitution, along with the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code, will soon bring the debate to a legislative closure.

sections.label: Youth poll on 377A repeal
sections.summary: A poll found 68% of youths saw repealing section 377A as positive for inclusivity, while respondents were divided on same-sex marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Almost seven in 10, or 68%, of youths polled said that the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code, which criminalises sex between homosexuals, is positive for inclusivity in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But when asked if same-sex marriage is wrong, the respondents were generally divided, with 37% agreeing or strongly agreeing with the statement, and 33% disagreeing or strongly disagreeing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the same time, 62% of the respondents felt that it was important to uphold and safeguard the definition of marriage as that between a man and a woman." There have been various polls done over time and, while they may not all be statistically significant, I believe they do sufficiently tell the story.

sections.label: Questions on churches preaching
sections.summary: An MP asks the Minister to clarify points on repealing section 377A, including whether Christian and Catholic Churches can still preach against gay sexual acts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we have heard in these past two days, the same is true for other religious communities and even for non-religious Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to ask the Minister to clarify a few points to help address concerns and worries in the minds and hearts of Singaporeans, even as we move to support the repeal of section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, will the Christian and Catholic Churches be assured that they will continue to be free to preach against gay sexual acts?

sections.label: MOE sexuality education in schools
sections.summary: An MP asks how MOE will handle sexuality education in public and private schools and protect Singapore's family and social norms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, how will MOE handle sexuality education in our schools, both public and private, and assure Singaporeans that Singapore's family and social norms, based on traditional Singaporean values, will be protected?

sections.label: Religious freedom and marriage norms
sections.summary: The passage states religious freedom to practise and teach beliefs will be maintained, and marriage as a union between a man and a woman will be upheld.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We will maintain our religious freedom to practise and teach what we believe to be right and wrong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We will uphold Singapore's societal norms where marriage is a union between a man and a woman and that married couples live as role models for their children and children's children.

sections.label: Survey on sexual minority youth
sections.summary: An NUS survey found 59% of 570 sexual minority young adults contemplated suicide and 14% attempted it, with section 377A hindering support groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A recent NUS public health survey found that among 570 sexual minority young adults aged 18 to 25, 59% had contemplated suicide and 14% had attempted to kill themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Having section 377A in our laws means that it is hard to organise support groups to help not just members of the gay community, which is who the laws target, but also the wider LGBTQ+ community, who face discrimination, bullying or mental struggles, just for being who they are.

sections.label: 377A and retaining LGBTQ talent
sections.summary: Section 377A made it challenging to convince prominent LGBTQ+ members in various sectors to remain in Singapore and contribute to society and the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Having section 377A made it challenging to convince prominent members of the LGBTQ+ community – Singaporean or otherwise – in the arts, financial sector, tech and many other areas to remain in Singapore and make meaningful contributions to our society and economy.

sections.label: Repeal of section 377A
sections.summary: A future Government could prosecute private consensual sex between men, so the speaker applauds repealing section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It also means that there is always a chance that a future Government may attempt to prosecute a man for sex with another man that was done in private and consensual.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That is why I applaud the Government's move to repeal section 377A.

sections.label: Dignity for marginalised Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker says repealing is not political but grants dignity and freedom to a marginalised section of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The ability to reach across the spaces between us, for dialogue and co-created understanding, is what will keep us safe." Mr Speaker, the issue of repealing, at its core, is not a political one but one that grants dignity and freedom to a marginalised section of Singapore.

sections.label: Constitutional amendment and marriage definition
sections.summary: The proposed constitutional amendment signals marriage is between a man and a woman, decided by legislature and society, not Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On the constitutional amendment that is being proposed, the message that Singapore sends is quite clear: the idea that marriage is only between a man and a woman and this is a decision that will be left for the legislature and society to decide, and not by the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As such, I do recognise the importance of the signal the new Article 156 sends, to provide greater protection for the definition of marriage and its related policies today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After the Prime Minister's announcement at the National Day Rally, MCI said that media policies on homosexuality will remain, which means, as a Toy Story Fan who has enjoyed the entire Toy Story series since 1995, I cannot bring my children to watch Lightyear, a Pixar animated children's film due to "overt homosexual depictions", as though homosexuality is unspeakable and cannot be seen.

sections.label: LGBTQ+ workplace survey findings
sections.summary: Surveys show many LGBTQ+ professionals value inclusive employers, and the speaker says all should contribute without discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A survey by YouGov in May 2022 on behalf of LinkedIn shared that 75% of LGBTQ+ professionals indicated that it is important that they work at a company where they feel comfortable bringing their full selves to work and 49% indicated that they will not work at a company that does not have LGBTQ+ friendly benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, a Deloitte survey of 600 members of the LGBTQ+ community across 12 countries showed that over 70% of the respondents are more inclined to remain with their current employer because of its approach to inclusiveness, while 37% of respondents indicate that they are actively considering changing employers to find one with a more inclusive culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Every individual in Singapore should be able to contribute in their fullest capacity without fear of being discriminated against for who they are – be it over race, language, religion, sexual orientation or gender identity.

sections.label: Support for repeal and amendment
sections.summary: A man married his partner though their marriage is not recognised in Singapore, and the speaker supports repeal and the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That is why he married his partner, even though he knows that their marriage is not recognised in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I support the repeal of section 377A and the Constitution (Amendment) Bill.

sections.label: Origins of section 377A
sections.summary: Section 377A was introduced in 1938 under colonial rule, with origins in Victorian times in the 1860s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Section 377A was first introduced in 1938, when Singapore was still part of the Straits Settlements and under colonial rule.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The origin of the provisions of section 377A stretched even further back to the Victorian times in the 1860s.

sections.label: Parliament debating section 377A challenges
sections.summary: The speaker says Parliament should debate risks from constitutional challenges to section 377A and has a duty to amend the Constitution to clarify marriage and family definitions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I think it is right for this Parliament of Singapore to debate and decide on the risks posed by recent constitutional challenges that our Court is also facing in terms of section 377A in our Penal Code, with the most recent one in just February this year in the case of Tan Seng Kee vs Attorney-General.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Suffice to say that I am of the view that this Parliament has the duty to set in place constitutional amendments to clarify our definitions of marriage and family.

sections.label: Nee Soon residents on 377A repeal
sections.summary: The speaker says residents fear repeal erodes marriage, family and children protections, and welcomes assurances that marriage definition and traditional family stance will not change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While majority of Singaporeans do not want to criminalise sex between gay men, residents I spoke to are concerned whether the repeal of section 377A will lead to an erosion of the protection for marriage, family and children and if the underlying motives of past legal challenges go beyond mere removal of stigma and criminalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that the Constitution (Amendment) Bill, which safeguards the definition of marriage without tying the hands of future generations, is a balanced approach to allow the Government of the day to consider prevailing societal attitudes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On this premise, my community at Nee Soon welcomes Prime Minister Lee and Deputy Prime Minister Wong's assurance that the definition of marriage will not change under their watch and the PAP Government's stance on the traditional family as a basic building block of our society will be strengthened while also respecting the dignity and place of gays in our community.

sections.label: Government position on workplace benefits
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government supports such arrangements and its position if gay couples push for more workplace benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government explain if it supports such arrangements and its position if gay couples were to push for more workplace benefits?

sections.label: Nation growing through diversity
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore has grown together by navigating this issue and can find strength and harmony in diversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In navigating and not avoiding this issue, we have grown together as a nation and I am confident that we can continue to find strength and harmony in diversity as we continue to write our Singapore story.

sections.label: Religious leaders' stated positions
sections.summary: The passage cites Cardinal William Goh on church neutrality and Mufti Nazirudin Mohd Nasir on Islam's stance and respecting differences.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I take heart by the stated positions of a number of our respected religious leaders earlier in August.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Then Archbishop, now Cardinal William Goh spoke of the Roman Catholic Church's neutrality on the repeal, provided that the church continues to have the freedom to teach what it believes and practise what it teaches.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mufti Nazirudin Mohd Nasir spoke of the complexity of the issue.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: He shared Islam's clear stance on sexuality and marriage and at the same time, the need to respect differences and keep our society cohesive and intact.

sections.label: Protecting marriage definition
sections.summary: The speaker says finding a way forward need not keep unenforced laws like section 377A nor redefine marriage and family, and marriage must be protected.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Finding a way forward does not mean we have to hold onto unenforced laws like section 377A, nor does it mean we have to redefine marriage and, consequently, family.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Since our families form the foundation of the moral and social fabric of Singapore, we must protect the definition of marriage to avoid more division amongst our people as lines get blurred.

sections.label: Common humanity and national unity
sections.summary: The passage urges going deeper into fuller human identity to acknowledge one another in common humanity and not give in to discord.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: On the repeal, let us remember that our sexual identity, while being an important aspect of our identity, is not the sum total of who we are.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: If we choose to go deeper into our fuller human identity, we will perhaps find connections that will help us acknowledge and understand one another in our common humanity.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Let us not give in to discord nor give up on unity but give our best to our nation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: May we then realise our commonalities, close the space between us and, together, discover the Singapore forward.

sections.label: Records of homosexual act convictions
sections.summary: The passage states records of egregious acts are unlikely to be spent, and there is no plan to proactively render spent records of persons convicted between 1988 and 2007.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But where egregious acts were committed, like non-consensual acts or sexual acts against minors, the records are unlikely to be treated as spent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There are a small number of individuals who were convicted between 1988 and 2007 for consensual, private, homosexual acts, between adults.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I have instructed my Ministry to consider how the records of these persons can be rendered spent proactively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The short answer is that there is no such plan.

sections.label: Article 156 and heterosexual marriage
sections.summary: The passage states Article 156 is structured to give effect to and protect laws and policies based on the heterosexual definition of marriage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Article 156 is structured to give effect to and protect laws and policies based on the heterosexual definition of marriage.

sections.label: Excluding Part 4 from challenge
sections.summary: The passage states that to protect the heterosexual definition of marriage from Court challenge, the whole of Part 4 has to be excluded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Members may think it is a little outside of the orthodox interpretation today, but can you rule it out?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Thus, if we want to properly protect the heterosexual definition of marriage from Court challenge, we have to exclude the whole of Part 4.

sections.label: Article 156 and banishment
sections.summary: The passage states Article 156 does not enable the Government to banish anyone as conventionally understood today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: To directly answer Mr Murali Pillai – no, Article 156 does not enable the Government to banish anyone as the term is conventionally understood today.

sections.label: Article 156 and elected branches
sections.summary: The passage states Article 156 takes the heterosexual definition of marriage and laws and policies based on it out from the Courts' province.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Article 156 takes two specific issues out from the Courts' province and keeps them entirely within the province of the elected branches: (a) the heterosexual definition of marriage and (b) the ability of the Parliament and Government to make laws and policies based on this definition.

sections.label: Parliament versus Courts on marriage
sections.summary: The passage frames the choice as Parliament deciding marriage issues or leaving them to the Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Ms Lim and Ms He's position would mean that they accept that the Courts can strike down the heterosexual definition of marriage or to curtail the ability of the Parliament and Government to make laws and policies based on this definition and for society to live with the consequences after that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This, then, is the choice before the House today – whether we decide to have the certainty that the Parliament will decide on issues of marriage or whether we want to leave this to the Courts and live with the potential threat of unconstitutionality and have that change imposed on our society, as has happened in other countries.

sections.label: Risks to section 377A and policies
sections.summary: It states risks that section 377A, the marriage definition and other policies could be challenged.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: One, section 377A is at risk of being struck out for being unconstitutional.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Two, if section 377A is struck out, then, there is a further risk that the definition of marriage could be challenged as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Three, and that then means that there are risks that our housing, education, media content policies and multiple other policies could all be challenged.

sections.label: PAP whip enables Parliament decision
sections.summary: It states a Parliament decision is possible only because the PAP has its whip in place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The only reason we can have a decision in Parliament is because the PAP has its whip in place.

sections.label: Policy stand and social cohesion
sections.summary: It says the policy balances views, maintains social cohesion, and the Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister will maintain this position.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And I think it is not too much to ask that a clear stand be taken on policy issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We believe that our policy offers a way forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It balances the different views, maintains our social cohesion, keeps us together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong have stated clearly that they will maintain this position.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: On this difficult matter, we will do our duty and take responsibility for holding society together.  .

sections.label: Inaction leaves legal risk
sections.summary: It states inaction leaves open the legal risk that the Court will rule section 377A unconstitutional.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Inaction will leave open the significant legal risk that the Court will, at some point in the future, rule section 377A unconstitutional.

sections.label: Article 156 and social norms
sections.summary: It states the Government intends no change in social norms after repeal, which Article 156 is intended to achieve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Mr Derrick Goh asked about the use of surveys and engagements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: It is indeed the intention of the Government that there should not be a change in social norms following the repeal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This is precisely what Article 156 is intended to achieve.

sections.label: Benefits for children of unwed parents
sections.summary: Children of single unwed and married parents receive equal benefits including healthcare, education subsidies, First Step grant, co-matching, and maternity leave for unwed mothers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Benefits intended to support a child’s development and caregiving are given to children of single unwed parents and of married parents equally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: These include healthcare and education subsidies, the Government’s First Step grant and co-matching of the Child Development Account, as well as the Government-paid maternity leave to unwed working mothers to care for their infant.

sections.label: Constitutional protection of marriage definition
sections.summary: Article 156 protects marriage as between a man and a woman, with no plans to include same-sex marriages, and solemnisers cannot solemnise same-sex couples.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: First, Article 156 will provide further protection for the definition of marriage as between a man and a woman.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: There are no plans to change this definition to include same-sex marriages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Religious leaders or any licensed solemniser for that matter, cannot solemnise a same-sex couple.

sections.label: Religious premises discretion on same-sex weddings
sections.summary: Religious organisations as owners of their premises may refuse to hold same-sex solemnisations or weddings on their premises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Religious organisations, as owners of their premises at places of worship, have the discretion to refuse same-sex solemnisations or weddings to be held on their premises.

sections.label: High bar for referenda
sections.summary: Referenda are required only when sovereignty or command of the Armed Forces and Police is at stake, with only one held on merger with Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Our Constitution sets a very high bar for the holding of referenda.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: A referendum is required when sovereignty or the command of our Armed Forces and Police is at stake.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
