sentences.text: We have only had one referendum in our history – on our merger with Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We should be very careful about elevating any matter to this level, saying it is equivalent to an issue on sovereignty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: It is the duty of elected Members of Parliament to consult, discuss and come to a decision even, and perhaps especially, for difficult and polarising social issues.

sections.label: Space for societal deliberation
sections.summary: Passing the two Bills created space for society to deliberate social issues within the political process, not through a zero-sum legal route.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: With the passing of the two Bills – the repeal of section 377A and the introduction of the constitutional amendment – we have created space for society to deliberate on social issues within the political process, and not through a legal route which is zero-sum in nature.

sections.label: Party positions on Bills
sections.summary: Six supported and three opposed repealing section 377A; on the Constitution, seven supported and two abstained, with Workers' Party MPs recording personal positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Six for the repeal of section 377A; three against, for reasons of conscience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The party position has now been established by way of a majority in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the Constitution, seven for and two abstentions for the reasons the Members mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All the Workers' Party MPs, apart from Mr Faisal Manap who is down with COVID-19, put their personal positions on the record.

sections.label: Whip on 377A repeal
sections.summary: The whip is imposed on repealing section 377A because it is a policy question with serious consequences for Singaporeans, and lifting it is not acceptable to the PAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When will a whip be lifted and when will a whip not be lifted?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I made it clear in this case, why is the whip being imposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is because it is a policy question with serious consequences for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we do not repeal section 377A, then we are saying we will not do what we have to do and we will pass on the buck to the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In such a situation, lifting the whip is not acceptable for the PAP because societal interests are at stake.

sections.label: Vote on constitutional amendment
sections.summary: They will vote no on the constitutional amendment because they want the definition of marriage decided by referendum rather than Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: As far as the vote for the constitutional amendment is concerned, we will be voting no, because of what I have explained earlier, that we would like the definition of marriage to be via referendum, rather than through Parliament.

sections.label: Support for referendum amendment
sections.summary: They will support a constitutional amendment if it says the definition of marriage is to be determined via national referendum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have to, reactively again, come to make a decision or wait for the Court to make that decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: We will support a constitutional amendment, if it says that the definition of marriage is to be determined via national referendum.

sections.label: Courts' role and abstention
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to confirm the Courts' constitutional role and says he is abstaining on the Constitution (Amendment) Bill, not opposing it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The third clarification is, I would like to ask the Minister to confirm that he accepts that the Courts have a constitutional role to ensure that Parliament's laws and Government actions do conform with the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And lastly, Sir, my clarification for the Constitution (Amendment) Bill, I did say that I am not opposing the Bill, but I am abstaining.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am concerned that that should be protected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I, for one, value it and that is why I am abstaining.

sections.label: Risk to section 377A
sections.summary: They take reference from what has happened elsewhere and agree there is a significant risk to section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think what we can see and what we need to take reference from is what has happened elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We agree that there is a significant risk to section 377A.

sections.label: Risk comparison of definitions
sections.summary: Once a risk is identified, chances should not be taken, and the risk to the heterosexual definition of marriage is less than the risk to section 377A.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Once you identify there is a risk, you then do not go and take chances.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, if one were to ask, "Is the risk to the heterosexual definition of marriage less than the risk to section 377A?", the answer is yes.

sections.label: Parliament decides marriage definition
sections.summary: The speaker says Parliament, not the Courts, can act, and that the risk of a challenge to the definition of marriage is a matter for Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We can do all of those things; the Courts cannot do those things.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is why we have decided there is this risk that the definition of marriage could be challenged and we have decided that is a matter for Parliament.

sections.label: Constitutional amendment and court jurisdiction
sections.summary: The speaker says this is not about avoiding the Courts' supervisory jurisdiction and believes most Singaporeans support the constitutional amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, this is not a case of, "Are we avoiding the supervisory jurisdiction of the Courts?" It has been explained.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I believe the overwhelming majority of Singaporeans support us on this constitutional amendment.

sections.label: Second Reading voting results
sections.summary: The Second Reading of the Bill was carried with 85 Ayes, two Noes and two Abstentions, by not less than two-thirds of Elected and Non-Constituency Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 85 "Ayes"; two "Noes"; and two "Abstentions".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Second Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament.    .

sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 85 "Ayes"; two "Noes"; and two "Abstentions".
